name: test
description:
1. Diagnosed a mismatch between the project shown in the ChatViewHeader and the project selected when creating a new sprint task.
2. Root cause #1: `SprintBoardModals.vue` only listened to `@select`, but `ProjectDetailt` emits its selection via `update:modelValue`, so `newTask.project_id` was never set.
3. Root cause #2: `ChatViewHeader.vue` rendered the parent `targetProject` prop instead of the chat's own working `project_id`, diverging from the sprint card.
4. Fix #1: Added `@update:model-value="onProjectSelected"` and hardened the handler to normalize object/id/string payloads and ignore stray events.
5. Fix #2: Added a `currentProject` computed in `ChatViewHeader.vue` that prefers `chat.project_id`, falling back to `owner_project_id` then the prop, so both views agree.

messages.content: When creating a new sprint task and selecting a working project, the proct shown in chatviewheader is not the same that the project shown in the sprint task. Analize and fix

## Analysis I traced the full path a sprint task's project takes from the “New Task” dialog to the chat header: | Step | File | Field | |------|------|-------| | 1. User picks a project in the dialog | `SprintBoardModals.vue` | `newTask.project_id` | | 2. Dialog emits the task | `SprintBoardModals.confirmNewTask` | `project_id` | | 3. Board persists it | `SprintBoardView.onTaskCreated` → `kanban.newSprintTask` | `project_id` (**working**) + `owner_project_id` (**where it lives**) | | 4. Chat header displays it | `ChatViewHeader.vue` | `targetProject` prop | I found **two independent defects** on this path — they are complementary, so both must be fixed: ### Defect 1 — the dialog never captures the selection `ProjectDetailt` is a `v-model` component (`modelValue` prop + `update:modelValue` event — that is how `ChatViewHeader.vue` uses it). The dialog, however, only listens to a `@select` event: ```vue ``` So `newTask.project_id` can stay `null`, the task is created against the **active/owner** project (`owner_project_id`) instead of the chosen working project, and the header shows the owner project. ### Defect 2 — the header trusts the prop instead of the chat `ChatViewHeader.vue` renders whatever `targetProject` the parent passes. A chat carries two projects: `owner_project_id` (where it is stored) and `project_id` (the **working** project you selected). The sprint card renders `chat.project_id`, but the header renders the prop — which resolves to the owner/active project. The header must prefer the chat's own working project so both surfaces agree. --- ## Fix 1 — `src/components/chat/ChatViewHeader.vue` Add a computed that resolves the chat's working project (falling back to the parent prop) and use it for both `ProjectDetailt` instances. ```vue src/components/chat/ChatViewHeader.vue ``` **Change summary** | Location | Before | After | |----------|--------|-------| | `computed` | `isMobile` only | added `currentProject` (chat project → prop → null) | | Mobile `ProjectDetailt` | `:modelValue="targetProject"` | `:modelValue="currentProject"` | | Desktop `ProjectDetailt` | `:modelValue="targetProject"` | `:modelValue="currentProject"` | --- ## Fix 2 — `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardModals.vue` Capture the project selection through the component's real `v-model` event (keeping `@select` for backward compatibility) and harden the handler so it only accepts payloads that resolve to a project id. ```vue src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardModals.vue ``` **Change summary** | Location | Before | After | |----------|--------|-------| | Project `ProjectDetailt` | `@select="onProjectSelected"` | `@update:model-value="onProjectSelected"` **(new)** + `@select="onProjectSelected"` (kept) | | `onProjectSelected(project)` | `this.newTask.project_id = project.project_id` | normalizes object/id/string and ignores stray payloads | --- ## Why this fixes it 1. **Selection is now captured** — the dialog writes the chosen project into `newTask.project_id`, so `confirmNewTask` emits the right `project_id`, and `kanban.newSprintTask` stores it as the chat's working `project_id` (while `owner_project_id` stays the sprint’s project). 2. **Header and card now agree** — `ChatViewHeader` renders `allProjectsById[chat.project_id]` (the *working* project the card shows) instead of a possibly-owner-scoped `targetProject`. ### Anti-patterns avoided - ❌ Relying on a single custom event name across two call-sites of the same component. - ❌ Displaying a prop that duplicates state already present on the entity (`chat.project_id`). - ❌ Blindly assigning `$event` without validating the payload shape. ### Accessibility note The project selector keeps its `focus:ring-2 focus:ring-primary/50`-style focus affordance and remains keyboard-operable; no interactive element or label was removed.
